analysis.title: October Payrolls: Labor Market Gains Steam
key_insights: October nonfarm payrolls rose 165,000, and the prior two months were revised up by a combined 84,000.
The three-month average of job creation rose from -45,000 in October 2025 to 137,000 in October 2026.
The three-month diffusion index is above 60%, which NISA reads as job growth broadening across the 250 private industries in the report.
The unemployment rate fell one tenth of a percent to 4.1%.

Construction employment fell 3,000 in October as labor shifts from residential to nonresidential work. NISA says data center construction labor demand is largely being met by excess labor from housing construction, which is struggling under elevated mortgage rates.
Construction wage growth is accelerating, partly because workers moving to nonresidential construction earn higher wages. Total wage inflation has so far stayed on its disinflationary path.
NISA says the labor market has rebounded from the weak conditions that led to the Fed's insurance cuts in 2025, and it sits in a zone that justifies neither cuts nor hikes.

NISA says the Fed is already on track to hike in December because of inflation concerns. It expects, with low conviction, that the Trump administration will find a way to lower oil prices in time to prevent a third hike in March.

NISA says whether the labor market justifies further tightening is a question for 2027. The answer depends partly on whether the newly elected political class constrains AI infrastructure investment, which has boosted labor demand this year.

sector_views.rationale: Residential construction employment is shrinking while nonresidential grows, with data center demand absorbed by labor released from housing. Construction wages are rising 5.2% y/y against 3.6% for all private workers.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Job growth is gaining momentum. The Fed is not pushed toward cuts, and NISA does not see enough strength to justify hikes.

risk_factors: Looming wage inflation if the labor market uptrend continues, which NISA does not yet see as enough to sway many FOMC votes.
An energy inflation shock keeping the Fed on a tightening path, with a third hike possible in March if oil prices stay high.
Political constraints on AI infrastructure investment could reduce labor demand.

tension_points.bull_case: Some will project the uptrend forward and warn of looming wage inflation, which would argue for further hikes.
tension_points.bear_case: NISA sees insufficient evidence of wage inflation to sway many FOMC votes, and construction wage acceleration has not pushed total wage growth off its disinflationary path.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Total wage inflation deviating from its disinflationary path, or oil prices staying high enough to force a third hike in March.
